title: Engineering Economics and Techno-Economic Analysis

models.group: Classical engineering economic equations and financial models
models.text: The suite should implement time value of money, compound interest, continuous compounding, present value, future value, equivalent annual worth, discounted cash flow, net present value, internal rate of return, modified internal rate of return, profitability index, benefit–cost ratio, return on investment, simple payback period, discounted payback period, equivalent annual cost and capital recovery factor methods.

models.group: Capital expenditure and cost estimation models
models.text: The suite should include bottom-up engineering cost estimation, analogous cost estimating, parametric cost estimating, unit-rate cost models, quantity-based estimation, equipment cost–capacity scaling, cost–capacity exponent models, learning curve models, experience curve models, factorial estimation, installation cost models, vessel day-rate models, procurement cost escalation, construction cost indices and probabilistic cost estimating.

The suite should implement lifecycle cost analysis, whole-life costing, total cost of ownership, discounted maintenance cost, reliability-centred maintenance economics, preventive maintenance optimization, corrective maintenance cost models, asset replacement analysis, optimal economic service life, residual value estimation and decommissioning liability modelling.

The suite should include production decline curve analysis, Arps exponential decline, Arps hyperbolic decline, Arps harmonic decline, capacity factor models, availability-adjusted production, energy yield calculations, production loss models, electricity revenue models, hydrocarbon price scenarios and stochastic commodity price forecasting.

The suite should implement levelized cost of energy, levelized cost of storage where applicable, levelized cost of delivered energy, avoided cost of energy, net energy production economics, capacity factor adjustments, degradation-adjusted energy yield, replacement cost models, renewable project cash-flow modelling and power purchase agreement revenue analysis.

The suite should incorporate weighted average cost of capital, capital asset pricing model, debt–equity financing, amortizing debt repayment, debt-service coverage ratio, loan life coverage ratio, project life coverage ratio, equity internal rate of return, project internal rate of return, tax depreciation, after-tax cash flow, inflation-adjusted valuation and real versus nominal discounting.

The suite should include probability distribution modelling, normal distributions, lognormal distributions, Weibull distributions, triangular distributions, PERT distributions, beta distributions, Monte Carlo simulation, Latin hypercube sampling, scenario analysis, sensitivity analysis, tornado diagram calculations, variance decomposition, Sobol sensitivity indices, value at risk, conditional value at risk, expected monetary value and probabilistic investment appraisal.

The suite should include Weibull failure-time models, exponential reliability models, lognormal lifetime models, renewal process theory, nonhomogeneous Poisson processes, Markov chains, semi-Markov models, fault-tree analysis, event-tree analysis, availability models, reliability block diagrams, mean time between failures, mean time to repair, expected downtime cost and reliability-centred inspection planning.

The suite should incorporate linear programming, nonlinear programming, mixed-integer linear programming, mixed-integer nonlinear programming, dynamic programming, stochastic programming, robust optimization, chance-constrained optimization, multi-objective optimization, genetic algorithms, differential evolution, particle swarm optimization, simulated annealing, Bayesian optimization and Pareto-front analysis.

models.group: Real options and strategic investment models
models.text: The suite should include real options valuation, binomial lattice models, Black–Scholes-type option methods where their assumptions are appropriate, decision-tree analysis, investment deferral models, staged development options, expansion options, abandonment options and flexibility valuation under uncertain future market conditions.

The suite should support autoregressive integrated moving average models, seasonal ARIMA, vector autoregression, state-space economic forecasting, Kalman filtering, generalized linear regression, multivariate regression, gradient boosting, random forests, Gaussian process regression, Bayesian hierarchical models and neural-network forecasting where sufficient trustworthy data are available.

The suite should combine physical engineering simulations with cost estimation, production forecasts, asset degradation models, operating availability, reliability calculations and discounted cash-flow economics. It should support coupled design–cost optimization, physics-based lifecycle assessment, stochastic project finance simulation, reliability-informed maintenance planning, Bayesian updating of cost forecasts, surrogate-assisted engineering optimization and multi-objective trade-off analysis covering cost, safety, technical performance, environmental effects and financial return.

subtitle: This additional suite should operate across the other 16 engineering suites. It should receive engineering results such as material quantities, installation schedules, energy production, equipment capacities, predicted maintenance requirements and structural design life, then convert them into financial and economic evaluations.
ic: The initial economic conditions shall define the project's financial position at the selected starting date, including initial capital investment, available equity, debt commitments, cash reserves, working capital and outstanding financial obligations.

For a new project, the initial state shall normally represent the pre-investment or investment-commitment stage, with the starting project valuation, construction schedule, capital requirements and financing structure established. For an existing asset, the initial conditions shall include the asset's current condition, remaining useful life, operating costs, historical expenditures, outstanding debt and forecast production capability.

The starting economic assumptions shall include the reference currency, price base year, inflation expectations, discount rate, applicable tax regime, depreciation treatment, project life and expected commercial revenue mechanism.

The initial production or energy-generation state shall be established from engineering performance forecasts. This may include expected hydrocarbon production, power generation, plant capacity, availability, maintenance requirements and anticipated degradation.

The initial uncertainty state shall define cost estimate distributions, commodity price scenarios, installation schedule uncertainty, equipment reliability assumptions and other relevant financial risks. For lifecycle analysis, the initial condition shall also distinguish costs already incurred from future expenditures included in the decision.
bc: The financial constraints shall specify the maximum available capital budget, borrowing limits, debt covenants, repayment obligations, liquidity requirements and minimum acceptable investment returns.

Revenue boundaries shall represent the relevant contract prices, power purchase agreements, hydrocarbon sales arrangements, transport tariffs, service fees or merchant-market assumptions. The model shall distinguish fixed contractual prices from externally varying market prices.
Cost boundaries shall include labour rates, equipment costs, marine vessel day rates, material prices, fuel costs, insurance costs, maintenance expenditure and applicable cost escalation assumptions.
Regulatory and fiscal constraints shall include tax rates, royalties, licensing obligations, environmental levies, depreciation rules and any legally applicable financial incentives.

Operational-economic constraints shall represent equipment availability, production capacity, allowable downtime, planned maintenance outages, project operating life and engineering performance limits provided by the other suites.
Investment optimization shall respect budget limits, minimum safety and performance requirements, maximum acceptable risk, required construction completion dates and applicable financing conditions.

At the end of the project evaluation, terminal conditions shall account for residual asset value, outstanding obligations, abandonment expenditure, decommissioning costs, site restoration and any relevant tax consequences.

Sensitivity and uncertainty analysis shall apply the specified boundaries of plausible cost, revenue, production, financing and schedule scenarios. Where these are probabilistic, the model shall use clearly defined probability distributions and correlation assumptions rather than treating every extreme value as simultaneously attainable.

calibration: Calibration should use historical project expenditure records, contractor quotations, supplier pricing, fabrication cost records, marine vessel day rates, operational expenditure records and completed project financial reports.

Capital cost estimation parameters should be calibrated using actual costs of comparable offshore structures, pipeline installations, renewable-energy systems, marine terminals and subsea developments. Differences in location, project scope, complexity, construction period, market conditions and procurement strategy should be explicitly accounted for.
Material cost models should be calibrated using historical procurement records, structural steel prices, concrete costs, specialized equipment quotations and actual fabrication expenditure.
Offshore installation cost models should use measured vessel productivity, mobilization costs, installation durations, marine spread costs and actual weather-related delays.

Operating expenditure models should be calibrated using recorded maintenance expenditure, vessel intervention costs, labour costs, inspection costs, fuel consumption, utility expenses and replacement equipment expenditure.

Production and revenue models should be calibrated using historical hydrocarbon production, renewable-energy generation, equipment availability, service demand and realized sales prices where applicable.
Asset degradation and maintenance cost models should be informed by observed component failure rates, maintenance schedules, actual replacement costs and documented downtime.
Financial assumptions should use appropriate market data, inflation information, financing terms, tax requirements and project-specific commercial arrangements.
Cost escalation and uncertainty models should be calibrated using historical variation between estimated and realized costs.
Calibration datasets should be segmented by project type and development period to avoid inappropriate comparisons between materially different industrial projects.
verification: All economic calculations should undergo independent arithmetic testing, automated unit tests, consistency checks and reconciliation of intermediate and final financial outputs.
Capital expenditure calculations should be checked for consistent treatment of quantities, unit costs, indirect costs, contingencies and escalation.
Operating expenditure calculations should be tested against controlled reference datasets covering fixed and variable operating costs.
Cash-flow timing should be verified to ensure that capital expenditure, operating expenditure, revenues, taxes, financing and decommissioning obligations occur in their intended periods.
Net present value calculations should be checked using independently established discounted cash-flow reference cases.
Internal rate of return calculations should be verified through reference cash-flow datasets, including cases with no valid rate or multiple possible rates.
Payback period, profitability index, return on investment and related economic indicators should be checked against independently calculated examples.
Levelized cost calculations should be verified for consistent energy production, project lifetime, cost timing, discounting and treatment of terminal costs.
Sensitivity analysis should be checked by varying one parameter at a time and confirming that the resulting financial calculations are reproducible.

Monte Carlo simulation and probabilistic uncertainty implementations should undergo random sampling tests, convergence studies, distribution checks and repeatability testing using controlled random seeds.
Optimization routines should be tested against simple benchmark problems with known optimum solutions and independently calculated constraints.
Currency conversion, inflation and financial escalation should be tested for consistent base dates, reference currencies and real versus nominal assumptions.
Database import, cost aggregation, reporting and project comparison functionality should undergo automated tests to detect missing values, duplicate entries and inconsistent cost categories.
validation: Capital cost predictions should be compared with independently completed offshore and marine engineering projects, using actual final expenditure rather than only early project budget estimates.
Fabrication and installation cost estimates should be evaluated against independently documented contractor expenditure and final account records.
Operating cost predictions should be compared with recorded expenditure from operating assets over representative periods.
Maintenance forecasts should be assessed against actual inspection, repair, replacement and offshore intervention records.
Production and revenue forecasts should be evaluated using subsequent independent operating and financial data.
Predicted installation durations and weather-related cost impacts should be compared with documented offshore construction schedules and actual delay records.

Levelized cost estimates should be evaluated against realized lifetime or sufficiently mature operating cost and production datasets, with uncertainty disclosed for assets that have not completed their operating lives.
Project cash-flow forecasts should be assessed against actual cash-flow performance, while distinguishing model error from changes in market prices, taxes, financing and project scope.
Cost uncertainty distributions should be evaluated using historical estimate-versus-actual outcomes and appropriate statistical coverage tests.
Optimization recommendations should be validated by comparing predicted benefits against independently evaluated engineering alternatives or implemented project changes.
Financial risk and sensitivity models should be assessed through historical scenario back-testing, forecast error analysis and comparison with realized project outcomes.

Validation should distinguish between accurate financial arithmetic and accurate economic forecasting. A mathematically correct investment model may still produce unreliable economic predictions if its cost, price, schedule and performance assumptions are not representative.
